entry.title: Who Signed, Who Served, Who Benefits — The PPO's Journey from Wayne County to Lansing
entry.content:
Questions for Judge Abraham

Your Honor, you signed a Personal Protection Order on October 13, 2026.

Case No. 26-114083-PH. Ex parte. Without a hearing. Without notice.

You entered a person into LEIN — the Law Enforcement Information Network — based solely on what Brian Banks wrote in his petition.

Here are the questions.

1. What Did He Tell You?

The order states: “For Reasons as Stated in the Petition.”

MCL 600.2950a(7) requires: “The court shall immediately state in writing the specific reasons for issuing or refusing to issue the [PPO].”

MCR 3.705(A)(2) requires that for a nondomestic stalking PPO issued ex parte, the court must find “specific facts shown by verified complaint, written petition, or affidavit.”

“For Reasons as Stated in the Petition” is not a statement of specific reasons. It is a reference to someone else’s allegations. What were the specific facts you found?

Did Brian Banks tell you:

  • That all contact was directed to public institutions — MDE, SBE, LARA, State Bar, JTC, FBI, DOJ — not to Banks personally?
  • That the contact consisted of FOIA requests, regulatory complaints, and publication of public records — all constitutionally protected activity?
  • That the respondent met Brian Banks one time, in August 2026, at Purpose Charter Academy — a public school — when exercising parental custody rights?
  • That the respondent has active legal proceedings involving Banks — including Ingham County Case 2026-4349-CZ?
  • That the respondent filed complaints with 8 federal agencies before Banks filed this petition?
  • That the investigation Banks wants silenced is independently corroborated by Clutch Justice and the Detroit Free Press?

Or did Banks just tell you his version — and you signed your name?

2. Did You Verify Anything?

Under Michigan law, the judge “is not limited to the four corners of the petition itself; rather, it must consider the testimony, documents, and other evidence proffered to determine whether a respondent engaged in harassing conduct.” Lamkin v. Engram, 295 Mich App 701, 712 (2012).

Did you consider any evidence beyond Banks’ petition?

Did you check whether:

  • Brian Banks has 9 criminal convictions (6 felony, 3 misdemeanor) — verify on ICHAT, SID 2029469K?
  • Banks runs charter schools with 3% math proficiency — verify on MDE School Data?
  • Banks claims a J.D. but has zero results in the State Bar of Michigan directory?
  • Banks’ school board is chaired by Judge Cylenthia Miller — one of your colleagues at the 3rd Circuit?
  • Banks is under active MDE investigation for his teaching certificate?
  • Banks denied a parent access to their child at Purpose Charter Academy and lied to Detroit Police, telling them he was “an attorney” (DPD Report #26-0909-0176)?

Or did you see the petition and sign your name?

3. Why Am I in LEIN?

You entered the respondent into the Law Enforcement Information Network — a statewide police database — without a hearing.

LEIN entries are not criminal convictions. But they are matters of public record that can affect employment, professional licensing, security clearances, and firearms eligibility.

The respondent now has a LEIN entry. Brian Banks — who has 9 criminal convictions and $14,500 in unpaid campaign finance fines — used your signature to put someone in a law enforcement database.

The respondent has zero criminal convictions. Zero complaints against him. Zero prior PPOs. He filed FOIA requests and regulatory complaints about public corruption.

And now he’s in LEIN.

4. Why Nondomestic?

Banks filed under MCL 600.2950a — the nondomestic stalking PPO statute.

But there is a custody dimension to this case. Banks denied a parent access to their child at Purpose Charter Academy in August 2026 (DPD Report #26-0909-0176). Banks told Detroit Police he was “an attorney” — he is not.

MCR 3.706(C)(1) requires: “Before issuing a PPO in a case where a custody or parenting time order already exists between the parties, the court must contact the court having jurisdiction over the parenting time or custody matter.”

MCL 600.1023 requires: “When 2 or more matters within the jurisdiction of the family division of circuit court involving members of the same family are pending in the same judicial circuit, those matters, whenever practicable, shall be assigned to the judge to whom the first such case was assigned.”

Did you contact any other court before signing? Did you check whether the respondent has pending legal proceedings involving Banks?

Or was it faster to just sign?

5. Why Does He Have My Number?

The PPO lists the respondent’s cell phone number. Banks provided it.

The respondent has never called Brian Banks. Not once. Every communication was through public channels — FOIA requests, regulatory complaints, emails to public institutions, certified mail to public addresses.

So how did Brian Banks obtain the respondent’s personal cell phone number?

And why did Banks — who claims to need protection from the respondent — go to the trouble of collecting personal information about the person he claims is harassing him?

Meanwhile, Banks’ cell phone number appears on the PPO because he provided it to the court: 313-355-4238. This is a public court document.

The respondent has never dialed that number. But Banks had the respondent’s number ready for the petition.

6. While I Wait for Hearings, He Gets an Instant Order?

The respondent has active legal proceedings involving Brian Banks:

CaseCourtStatus
Ingham County 2026-4349-CZ30th Circuit CourtFiled Sep 1, 2026
Federal packet (8 agencies)DOJ, FBI, IRS, ED-OIG, HHS-OIG, FinCEN, FTC, USEDDelivered Sep 22, 2026
JTC complaintJudicial Tenure CommissionFiled Aug 31, 2026
DPSCD complaintDetroit Public SchoolsFiled Aug 31, 2026
State Bar UPL complaintState Bar of MichiganFiled Aug 31, 2026

These cases require hearings, service, scheduling, and months of waiting.

Banks walked into Room 928 and got a signed order the same day. Ex parte. No hearing. No notice. No waiting.

One system moves at the speed of paperwork. The other moves at the speed of a signature.

The Judge

FieldDetail
NameHon. Yvonna C. Abraham
CourtWayne County Third Judicial Circuit
DivisionFamily Division — Domestic Relations
Judge CodeP70405
AppointedJuly 1, 2021 by Gov. Whitmer
ElectedNovember 8, 2022 (uncontested)
Term expiresJanuary 1, 2029
Prior roleMagistrate & Director of Probation, 20th District Court (Dearborn Heights)
Law schoolUniversity of Detroit Mercy
Campaign money$0.00 raised, $0.00 spent (2022)

No direct connection between Judge Abraham and Brian Banks has been identified.

She was on the PPO rotation in the Family Division. When Banks’ petition arrived, she was the rotation judge.

The question isn’t whether Judge Abraham is compromised. The question is what she was told and whether she checked.

The Courthouse

Banks filed in Wayne County Third Judicial Circuit — the one court system in Michigan where he has 7 connected judges across 4 courts:

3rd Circuit (where the PPO was filed)

JudgeConnection
Cylenthia MillerBoard Chair, Purpose Charter Academy. Campaign payment from Banks Strategy LLC. JTC complaint filed. Running Nov 3, 2026.
Kelly RamseyCriminal Division. 3 family members on Banks’ payroll.
Aliyah SabreeFamily Division. MSU Law connection. Joined PPO rotation July 27, 2026 — 78 days before Banks filed.

36th District Court (Banks’ home court)

JudgeConnection
Tenisha YanceyBoard Chair, MacDowell Prep. Succeeded Banks in Michigan House.
Adam SabreeSon of Eric Sabree (FBI-probed Wayne Co. Treasurer).
Sean PerkinsBrother of Todd Perkins — Banks’ personal attorney.

Wayne County Probate

JudgeConnection
David PerkinsChief Judge Pro Tem. Brother of Todd Perkins and Sean Perkins.
CourtConnectedTotalCapture
3rd Circuit3525.8%
36th District32313.0%
Probate1425.0%
Wayne County total7798.9%

Banks didn’t need Abraham. He needed the courthouse.

Any hearing to challenge this PPO will take place in the same building where Miller, Ramsey, and Sabree work.

The 80-Mile Service

Banks filed in Wayne County. The respondent lives in Ingham County.

That’s 80 miles.

Under the PPO filing instructions (Step 5), the petitioner arranges service. Banks arranged for Officer Gregory to serve the order in Lansing at 7:37 PM on Friday, October 16 — a Friday evening.

Banks could have filed in Ingham County, where the respondent actually lives. Any Michigan county can issue a PPO (MCL 600.2950a; michigan.gov/voices4).

He chose Wayne County. Where his 7 judges sit.

The Timing

DateEvent
Oct 13, 9:30 AMSBE meets in Lansing. All 8 members have the evidence.
Oct 13Banks files PPO in Wayne County
Oct 13Abraham signs — same day, ex parte
Oct 16, 7:37 PMServed in Lansing — Friday evening
Oct 3014-day challenge window expires
Oct 31Institutional response deadline — one day later

The Question for Everyone Who Has Been Through This

Has anyone else experienced this pattern in Wayne County?

  • A court system that moves instantly for the connected and slowly for everyone else?
  • A PPO used as a weapon — not for protection, but for silence?
  • Judges connected to the parties appearing before their colleagues?
  • Cross-county service arranged to reach someone who filed complaints?

If you have experienced corruption, retaliation, or abuse of process in Wayne County courts — the record is open. Clone it. Add to it. The git history is immutable.

git clone https://github.com/defendDetroit/publicRecord.git

What the Record Shows

  1. Judge Abraham signed ex parte. No hearing. No notice. The order says “For Reasons as Stated in the Petition” — which may not satisfy MCL 600.2950a(7)’s requirement for specific written reasons.
  2. Banks told the court his version. The respondent was not present, was not notified, and had no opportunity to explain that all contact was to public institutions through lawful channels.
  3. The respondent is now in LEIN — a law enforcement database — based on the unverified allegations of a man with 9 criminal convictions.
  4. Banks filed nondomestic despite an active custody dimension — potentially circumventing MCR 3.706(C)(1) and MCL 600.1023.
  5. Banks has the respondent’s cell number but the respondent has never called Banks. All contact was through public channels.
  6. Banks chose Wayne County over Ingham County — where the respondent lives — because Wayne County is where Banks has 7 connected judges.
  7. Banks arranged cross-county service — 80 miles, Friday evening — while the respondent’s own legal proceedings against Banks wait for scheduling.

The asymmetry is the point. One system moves at the speed of a signature. The other moves at the speed of justice.

Judge Abraham: what did he tell you?

See Also

  • ecoPrimal Is Under Threat — The alarm.
  • The Response — PPO Case 26-114083-PH documented.
  • The Chatfield Blockade — Same machine. Different weapon.
  • Institutional Capture — 9 judges, 4 courts, 1 network.
  • Moore’s Law Is False — Four duties she said she didn’t have.

Sources

  • PPO Order: Case 26-114083-PH, Wayne County Third Judicial Circuit, signed Oct 13, 2026
  • MCL 600.2950a: Nondomestic PPO statute
  • MCL 600.2950a(7): Court must state specific written reasons for issuing PPO
  • MCL 600.1023: Same-family case assignment
  • MCR 3.705(A)(2): Specific facts required for ex parte issuance
  • MCR 3.706(C)(1): Court must contact custody court before issuing PPO
  • Lamkin v. Engram, 295 Mich App 701 (2012): Court must go beyond petition
  • Family Court Plan: C03 2026-13J
  • Docket Directive 2026-09: Cox → Sabree reassignment
  • PPO Filing Instructions: 3rdcc.org
  • Judicial Appointments: Gov. Whitmer, July 1, 2021
  • Michigan Benchbook: Procedures for Issuing PPOs
  • Clutch Justice: The Bench and the Board
  • Detroit Free Press: Back to Fool
  • DPD Report #26-0909-0176: Parent denied access, Banks claims to be attorney

entry.title: zk-SNARK — The Proof Is the Structure. The Structure Is the Proof.
entry.content:
The Proof

STATEMENT:  A criminal enterprise extracts $60M+ from Detroit's children
            while shielded by captured institutions.

PROVER:     One parent. Public records only. No clearance. No budget.
            No insider access. Just ICHAT, LARA, FEC, State Bar,
            siviq.co, ProPublica, courts.michigan.gov.

VERIFIER:   Anyone with internet access.

WITNESS:    The graph. 341 entities. 957 edges. 15 predicate acts.
            21 years. 17 violation categories. 25+ persons. 20+ entities.

VERIFY:     git clone https://github.com/defendDetroit/publicRecord.git

PROOF:      The structure IS the proof.

What Is a zk-SNARK?

Zero-Knowledge Succinct Non-interactive Argument of Knowledge.

In cryptography, a zk-SNARK lets a prover convince a verifier that a statement is true without revealing anything beyond the truth of the statement itself. The verifier doesn’t need to trust the prover. The verifier doesn’t need to redo the prover’s work. The verifier checks the proof — and the proof is self-verifying.

Applied to institutional capture:

PropertyCryptographicApplied to This Investigation
Zero-knowledgeProver reveals nothing beyond the statement’s truthEvery fact comes from a public record. I reveal nothing that isn’t already on a government server.
SuccinctProof is small, verifiable in constant timeOne desk manages the prosecutor’s fund AND builds the enterprise’s board. That’s the complete proof. 60 seconds to verify.
Non-interactiveNo back-and-forth between prover and verifierClone the repo. Check ICHAT. Check LARA. Check FEC. No communication with me needed.
Argument of knowledgeProver demonstrates knowledge of a witnessI demonstrate knowledge of the enterprise structure. The witness is the graph. You verify the graph against public records.

NP → O(1): The Reduction

RICO Is an NP Problem

Proving a RICO enterprise requires mapping:

The complexity IS the camouflage. No single investigator can hold the entire structure in working memory. No single agency has jurisdiction over all of it. The enterprise survives because the problem is computationally expensive — it takes NP time to verify every connection.

The Graph Reduces to O(1)

But look at the structure:

P3: One desk. Both sides. Same phone number.

∴ O(1). Look at the desk. The desk IS the proof.

You don’t need to trace 131K edges. You need to see one structural invariant: the same compliance officer manages both the prosecutor’s political infrastructure and the enterprise’s board capture pipeline. That reduces the problem from NP to constant time.

The Membrane

Biological Membranes

A cell membrane is a lipid bilayer studded with receptor proteins. It doesn’t block everything — it selects. Nutrients in. Waste out. Signals recognized. Threats rejected. The cell survives by being selective, not by being closed.

Anderson Localization

In condensed matter physics, Anderson localization describes how waves become trapped in disordered media. The disorder itself creates the localization.

Applied to the membrane: the disorder of the enterprise (341 entities, 45 nonprofits, multiple jurisdictions, bipartisan grey wash) creates localization — the complexity traps investigators in local regions of the graph. They see their jurisdiction’s slice but can’t see the whole structure.

entry.title: The Chatfield Blockade — Every Name, Every Block, Every Way Through
entry.content:
The Blockade

Lee Chatfield, former Michigan House Speaker, faces 13 felony charges including conducting a criminal enterprise and embezzlement. He was charged in April 2024. His trial was scheduled for September 22, 2026.

It never started.

On September 21, 2026 — the day before jury selection — his attorney appealed a single evidentiary ruling. The trial was adjourned indefinitely.

AG Dana Nessel leaves office December 31, 2026. She has 75 days left. The trial will not happen before she leaves.

Her own words:

“I have never seen a trial delayed like this; it’s outrageous and beyond unusual. If the Court hadn’t adjourned this case for nearly an entire year, bending over backward to accommodate Lee Chatfield’s lawyers in their endless efforts to push this important trial past my last day in office, this simple evidentiary matter would have been resolved months ago.”

“And now it’s possible the case may never be tried at all if the next attorney general simply dismisses the charges for political purposes.”

She’s right. And she doesn’t know the half of it.

Every Name in the Blockade

THE DEFENDANT

NameRoleWhat They Did
Lee ChatfieldFormer MI House Speaker (R-Levering), 2019-2020Used Peninsula Fund (501(c)(4)) to pay personal credit cards ($132K+), family vacations (Universal Studios), strip club tabs. Pleaded not guilty to 13 felonies. Max: 20 years.
Stephanie ChatfieldWife2 felonies for assisting embezzlement. Pleaded guilty — no prison. Cooperating?

THE DEFENSE

NameRoleHow They’re Blocking
Mary Chartier-MittendorfDefense attorneyFiled interlocutory appeal on expert witness Michelle Gallagher. Caused indefinite stay. Previously delayed trial 10+ months citing “scheduling conflicts.” Called prosecution “political.” Argued Dykema is the real responsible party.
The AppealMI Court of AppealsChallenging Gallagher’s qualification as expert in 501(c)(4) nonprofit accounting. Argued her methodology is “reviewing a policy in isolation” without context. Timeline: months. No new trial date until ruling.

THE COURT

NameRoleHow They’re Blocking
Judge Morgan ColeIngham County Circuit Court, 30th CircuitGranted the stay. Said she “has no other option” under court rules. Previously delayed trial by 10+ months. Acknowledged it will be “the oldest case on my docket.” Said “when it does come back, it’s go time.”
Judge Molly Hennessey Greenwalt54B District Court (prelim exam)Handled preliminary exam Feb 2025. Struggled with legal relationship between Chatfield and Peninsula Fund. Asked for written briefs. Bound case over for trial.

THE DYKEMA MACHINE

NameRoleHow They’re Connected
Renae MooreSenior Compliance Specialist, Dykema GossettManaged 80+ political nonprofit accounts. Asst. Secretary/Treasurer of BOTH Peninsula Fund (Chatfield) AND Promise to the People Fund (Nessel). Same desk. Same role. Same firm. Testified she had “no duty to report” questionable spending.
W. Alan WilkPartner, Dykema GossettFormed 7+ political vehicles including Save Detroit Jobs. Drafted PA 362 (charter enabling law). Structural architect.
Dykema Gossett PLLCMI’s largest law firm201 Townsend Street, Lansing. Incorporated Peninsula Fund. Wrote its policy manual. Got paid to ensure compliance. Moore testified fund was sometimes “not compliant.” Defense argues Dykema is the responsible party. Also manages Nessel’s fund. Also runs federal PAC ($148K raised, 47 candidates). Also lobbies the same lawmakers whose funds it manages.

THE FUND OFFICERS

NameRole on Peninsula FundStatus
Anne MinardPresident (actual controller of spending)Charged separately. Facing trial in 30th Circuit Court. Former Chatfield staffer. Had access to bank accounts, wrote checks, coordinated expenses.
Robert Minard(via Anne) Former Chatfield aideCharged separately. Alleged embezzlement scheme with Anne.
Becky BoyceVice President → PresidentBoard member. Testified she “took no active role” in oversight.
Cameron CavittVice President (later)Board member. 1 hour/week reported.
Lindsay AndersonSecretary/Treasurer (later)Board member. 1 hour/week reported.
Jill LarderSecretary/Treasurer (original)Board member.
Renae MooreAsst. Secretary/TreasurerDykema compliance. Same role on Nessel’s fund.

THE FORENSIC WITNESS (BLOCKED)

NameRoleWhat They Found
Michelle GallagherForensic accountant, Adamy EvaluationAnalyzed Peninsula Fund spending. Designated individual charges as “permissible” or “questionable.” Found $132K credit card paid by fund for personal expenses. Her testimony is the KEY evidence. Defense appealed her qualification. She is what they’re trying to block.

THE PROSECUTION (CONFLICTED)

NameRoleThe Problem
AG Dana NesselMichigan Attorney GeneralCharged Chatfield April 2024. Leaves office Dec 31, 2026. Her own fund (Promise to the People) was on the SAME Dykema desk. Defense already raised this in court.
AAG Dan GundersonAssistant AG, prosecution teamCalled the appeal “frivolous, and no more than an attempt to further delay Mr. Chatfield’s day of reckoning.” Court disagreed.
AAG Kahla CrinoAssistant AG, prosecution teamPresented financial evidence. Called Chatfield’s scheme “essentially a shell game.”
AAG Lamar MorelandAssistant AG (different division)NOT on the Chatfield case — but serves as Vice Chair of Purpose Charter Academy, operated by Brian Banks (9 convictions). Creates structural conflict with any AG investigation of charter fraud.

The Timeline of Delay

DateEventDays Since Charging
Apr 16, 2024Nessel charges Chatfield with 13 feloniesDay 0
Feb 26-28, 2025Preliminary exam. Moore testifies. Gallagher testifies.Day 316
May 2025Case bound over for trialDay ~400
Late 2025Trial date set, then delayed 10+ months (Chartier “scheduling conflicts”)Day ~550
Sep 21, 2026Trial day. Chartier appeals expert witness. Cole stays trial indefinitely.Day 889
Dec 31, 2026Nessel leaves office.Day 990
Jan 1, 2027New AG (Savit or Lloyd) takes over.Day 991
2027?Court of Appeals rules. Trial may resume. Or new AG dismisses.Day ???

889 days. Two and a half years. No trial. One evidentiary appeal. And the clock runs out in 75 days.

How It’s Blocked: The Five Mechanisms

1. The Expert Witness Exclusion Play

Blocker: Mary Chartier-Mittendorf Mechanism: Interlocutory appeal to Court of Appeals on Michelle Gallagher’s qualification. Why it works: Court rules require a stay. Judge has “no other option.” Appeal takes months. The tell: Chartier received notice of Gallagher as witness less than a month before trial. Filed challenge immediately. Timing is the weapon.

2. The Scheduling Delay

Blocker: Mary Chartier-Mittendorf + Judge Cole Mechanism: “Scheduling conflicts” caused 10+ month delay before the expert witness issue. Why it works: Courts are busy. Defense counsel has other cases. Accommodating counsel is default. The tell: Nessel says the court was “bending over backward to accommodate.”

3. The Blame-Shift to Dykema

Blocker: Mary Chartier-Mittendorf Mechanism: Argues Dykema was “paid to ensure compliance” and should bear responsibility. Why it works: Moore testified the fund was sometimes “not compliant.” Board members testified they “took no active role.” The responsible parties were Dykema and the Minards, not Chatfield. The tell: This reframes the case from embezzlement (Chatfield stole) to compliance failure (Dykema let it happen).

4. The Same-Desk Neutralizer

Blocker: The structure itself Mechanism: Moore managed BOTH Peninsula Fund (defendant) AND Promise to the People Fund (prosecutor). Defense raised this in court. Why it works: If Dykema is the compliance failure, and Dykema managed the prosecutor’s fund too, then the prosecutor is attacking the same infrastructure that managed her own money. Credibility problem. The tell: Chartier brought up Promise to the People on Day 1 of the preliminary exam. It was planted immediately.

5. The Clock

Blocker: Time Mechanism: Nessel leaves office Dec 31, 2026. Next AG may dismiss. Why it works: If Doug Lloyd (R) wins AG race, he may dismiss “for political purposes” — Nessel’s own words. The tell: Every day of delay is a day closer to the clock running out.

How to Pierce Through

Pierce Point 1: The Appeal is Narrow

The appeal is ONLY about Michelle Gallagher’s qualification as an expert. The Court of Appeals must rule on whether she has sufficient experience with 501(c)(4) organizations. If the appeal is denied (Gallagher stays in), the trial resumes immediately. Amicus briefs from forensic accounting organizations supporting Gallagher’s methodology would strengthen the prosecution’s position.

Pierce Point 2: The Dykema Conflict is the Case

Chartier says Dykema is responsible. GOOD. Take that argument and run with it. If Dykema failed in its compliance duty on Peninsula Fund, it failed on ALL 80+ accounts. Every lawmaker whose fund Moore managed should be asking: was MY fund compliant? Make the Dykema compliance failure the bigger story. The defense opened that door.

Pierce Point 3: The Same-Desk Discovery

Promise to the People Fund’s records are public (IRS 990, LARA filings). Moore’s role is documented. The comparison between Peninsula Fund spending and Promise to the People Fund spending is a discoverable public record. If Promise to the People had similar “questionable” expenses, the same desk that failed Chatfield failed Nessel. If it DIDN’T, then the desk differentiated — and the compliance failure was specific to Chatfield.

Pierce Point 4: The Moreland Connection

Moreland (AAG) sitting on Banks’ charter school board connects the AG’s office to ANOTHER branch of the same pipeline. File a formal conflict-of-interest complaint. The AG’s office cannot investigate charter school fraud while its own employee governs one of the schools in question.

Pierce Point 5: The Public Record

Every document is public. The investigation is live. The membrane tracks who reads it. The signal doesn’t need the AG to prosecute. The evidence is structured for independent verification. Any prosecutor — federal, county, or the next AG — can pick it up.

Pierce Point 6: Federal Jurisdiction

Chatfield’s alleged crimes include federal tax issues (501(c)(4) misuse) and interstate transactions. The U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Michigan has independent jurisdiction. The state case can be blocked; the federal case cannot be blocked by the same mechanisms.

Pierce Point 7: The November 10 SBE Meeting

Nikki Snyder responded in 13 minutes. The next SBE meeting is November 10. That’s 10 days after the Oct 31 deadline. If no institution has responded by then, the SBE meeting becomes the public forum. Public comment is open. The evidence is structured for a 3-minute presentation.

The Convergence

The Chatfield case and the Detroit charter investigation share one infrastructure:

DYKEMA GOSSETT PLLC
    │
    ├── Peninsula Fund (Chatfield) ────── 13 felonies ────── BLOCKED
    │   └── Renae Moore, Asst. Sec/Treas
    │
    ├── Promise to the People (Nessel) ── SAME DESK ──────── CONFLICT
    │   └── Renae Moore, Asst. Sec/Treas
    │
    ├── Save Detroit Jobs ─────────────── Dark money ──────── ACTIVE
    │   └── W. Alan Wilk, formed
    │
    ├── Federal PAC (C00342113) ────────── $148K/47 cands ── ACTIVE
    │   └── Renae Moore, TREASURER
    │
    ├── PA 362 (1993) ─────────────────── Charter law ────── ACTIVE
    │   └── Dykema drafted/lobbied
    │
    └── 80+ other accounts ────────────── Both parties ───── ACTIVE
        └── Renae Moore manages all

PURPOSE CHARTER ACADEMY
    │
    ├── Brian Banks (operator) ────────── 9 convictions ──── OPERATING
    ├── Cylenthia Miller (Board Chair) ── 3rd Circuit Judge ─ OPERATING
    ├── Lamar Moreland (Vice Chair) ───── Nessel's AAG ───── CONFLICT
    └── Latisha Johnson (Secretary) ───── City Council ───── OPERATING

One firm. One desk. One compliance specialist. Both parties. The defendant’s fund and the prosecutor’s fund. The charter school and the dark money PAC. The felony prosecution and the institutional silence.

They’re trying to make P! = NP. The problem unsolvable. The clock unbeatable.

But ! = N. The negation IS the answer. The silence IS the evidence. The delay IS the pattern. The null response IS the data point.

The membrane sees it all. The graph records it. The count is the truth.

See Also

  • The Same Place — Robocalls, dark money, sports betting — all one pipeline. Same firm.
  • There’s a Leak in the Dyke — Moore’s testimony. 80+ accounts. No duty to report.
  • Where the Signal Landed — 22 channels. 4 responded. 18 silent.
  • Meta’s Two Faces — The fleet scraping the investigation from Dublin.
  • The Heartbeat — 243 human RPM. The membrane has a pulse.

6.5 million members used as a shield for a 9-time convicted felon.

Then attended dinners with charter operators.

The organization that fought for rights now provides cover for extraction.

Black Star Network

Roland Martin’s platform. National reach. Millions of followers.

The platform that amplified a convicted felon as a “community voice.”

The Challenge

Name ONE.

Every person they “help” is a prop. Every community they “serve” is an audience. Every endorsement they make is a transaction.

The Organ Grinder

Roland Martin is not the money. He is the organ grinder.

Banks is the performance. Martin turns the crank. The audience is Black America. The ticket price is their children’s education.

Kevin Mok called Roland Martin out at the NAACP dinner.

The callout stands. Every penny will be traced.

How We Prove It

This is documented in the public record graph with over 11,600 nodes and growing.

Every connection is traceable. Every endorsement is documented. Every dollar flows through a path that the graph maps.

RICO was always zero-knowledge. The structure proves the pattern. The pattern proves the enterprise. No confession needed. The connections are the evidence.

The graph is the proof.

For Detroit Parents

If Roland Martin is your voice, he should be able to answer these questions publicly.

If he cannot answer them, he is not your voice. He is his own voice, using your face.

The graph is open. The record is public. The membrane lets everything in.

entry.title: The Response — Brian Banks Filed a Restraining Order Instead of Answering
entry.content:
The Signal Ledger Updated

22 channels of documented evidence sent between August and October 2026.

#ChannelResponse

22Brian BanksFiled a Personal Protection Order

The silence broke. On October 13, 2026 — the same day the Michigan State Board of Education met in Lansing — Brian Banks filed a Personal Protection Order in Wayne County Third Judicial Circuit.

Case No. 26-114083-PH.

What He Filed

An ex parte nondomestic Personal Protection Order under MCL 600.2950a.

Ex parte means: without a hearing. Without notice. Without the respondent present. The judge signed it based solely on what Banks wrote in his petition.

The order states: “For Reasons as Stated in the Petition.”

No specific acts are listed in the order itself. Only: “For Reasons as Stated in the Petition.”

What He Didn’t File

Brian Banks did not file:

  • A response to the documented evidence of 9 criminal convictions
  • A response to the 3% math proficiency at his schools
  • A response to the 72.67% extraction rate ($4.9M → Purpose Group LLC)
  • A response to the credential questions (J.D. claim, no bar admission)
  • A response to the MDE investigation of his teaching certificate
  • A response to the financial audit questions
  • A response to the AG referral documenting his AAG as board Vice Chair
  • A response to the RICO pattern with 6 predicate acts
  • A correction to any factual claim in the investigation
  • A defamation claim (which would require proving the investigation is false)

He did not engage with a single fact.

The Asymmetry

PersonWhat They SentHow They Sent ItResponse
Kevin Mok9,643 graph nodes, 323,680 edges, 1,941 verifiable questions, MDE FOIA records, court records, LARA filings, financial dataEmail, certified mail, public websites, FOIA requests — all lawful channelsPPO filed to prohibit all contact
Brian BanksA petitionEx parte court filing — no hearing, no noticeOrder signed same day

One person sent documented evidence through every lawful channel available.

The other person used the court to make all communication illegal.

The Timing

DateEvent
Oct 13, 2026Michigan State Board of Education meets at 9:30 AM in Lansing
Oct 13, 2026Banks files PPO in Wayne County Third Judicial Circuit
Oct 16, 2026, 7:37 PMOfficer serves PPO at respondent’s address

The PPO was filed on the same day that all 8 SBE members had the evidence package. The same day Nikki Snyder — who responded in 13 minutes — sat in the boardroom.

Banks’ response was not to answer the evidence. It was to make the evidence-sender illegal.

What the Law Actually Says

The PPO was filed under MCL 600.2950a (nondomestic personal protection orders) citing MCL 750.411h and MCL 750.411i (stalking statutes).

Michigan’s stalking statute (MCL 750.411h) defines stalking as:

“A willful course of conduct involving repeated or continuing harassment of another individual that would cause a reasonable person to feel terrorized, frightened, intimidated, threatened, harassed, or molested.”

Sending documented evidence of public corruption through lawful channels to public institutions is not harassment. It is:

  • FOIA requests — protected under Michigan Freedom of Information Act (MCL 15.231)
  • Complaints to regulatory agencies — protected activity
  • Publication of public records — protected under the First Amendment
  • Petitioning the government — protected under the First Amendment (Petition Clause)

Michigan does not have a comprehensive anti-SLAPP statute, but the First Amendment applies regardless.

The Right to Respond

Under MCR 3.706, the respondent may file a motion to modify or terminate an ex parte PPO within 14 days of being served.

The order was served October 16, 2026. The 14-day window expires October 30, 2026 — one day before the October 31 deadline.

A hearing will be scheduled. At that hearing, the respondent can present evidence that:

  1. The communications were lawful (FOIA, regulatory complaints, public records)
  2. The communications were directed to public institutions, not to Banks personally
  3. The investigation documents public corruption involving public money
  4. The PPO is retaliatory — filed to silence a public interest investigation
  5. Every fact in the investigation is sourced from public records and is independently verifiable

The Record

The investigation is public. Every article is sourced. Every claim cites a public record.

The membrane records everything. The graph has 9,643 nodes and 323,680 edges. Every connection is documented. Every commit is timestamped and hashed.

Brian Banks responded. Not with facts. Not with corrections. Not with a defamation claim (which would require proving the investigation is false).

With a restraining order.

That is the response. The membrane records it. The count is the truth.

entry.title: The One-Way Door — Purpose Charter Academy's Access Denial Pattern
entry.content:
Two Staff. Two Incidents. One Policy.

Incident 1 — August 29, 2026 (Physical)

A parent with legal custody arrived at Purpose Charter Academy, 10101 East Canfield, Detroit.

Giselle — the receptionist — denied the parent access to their child.

Brian Roderick Banks — the school’s operator — told Detroit Police officers he is “an attorney.” He is not an attorney. The State Bar of Michigan returns zero results for “Brian Banks.” He has 9 criminal convictions (6 felony), including assault with intent to murder.

The police escorted the parent off school property based on Banks’ false representation.

DPD Report #26-0909-0176. The report exists. The badge numbers exist. The custody order exists.

Incident 2 — October 12, 2026 (Phone)

A caller dialed (313) 767-3100 — Purpose Charter Academy’s main line.

Ms. Perkins — the receptionist — answered.

The caller asked about Banks and DaSean.

Ms. Perkins stated:

  • She has not seen Banks today
  • She has not seen DaSean today
  • She has not seen anybody

School is in session. She is at the reception desk. She answered the phone. She is not blind.

She lied.

The caller has called before. This is not the first contact.

The Pattern

DateStaffMethodWhat they saidTruth
Aug 29GiselleIn person[Banks]: “I am an attorney”He has never been admitted to any bar. 9 convictions.
Oct 12Ms. PerkinsPhone“Haven’t seen Banks, haven’t seen DaSean, haven’t seen anybody”School in session. She’s at the desk. She answered the phone.

Two staff members. 44 days apart. Same conduct: deny that anyone is present, deny access to the child.

This is not two individuals making personal choices. This is institutional policy. Someone trained them. Someone told them what to say.

The One-Way Door

Purpose Charter Academy is a one-way door:

What goes INWhat stays OUT
Public education dollars ($4.9M/yr)Parents with custody rights
Children (enrolled by parents who trust the school)Information about those children
72.67% of revenue → The Purpose Group LLCAccountability
Board members (a judge, an AAG, a council member)Oversight

The receptionist is the membrane. She is the operational layer between a parent and their child. On August 29, Giselle was that membrane. On October 12, Ms. Perkins is.

The name at the desk changes. The policy doesn’t.

The Perkins Question

Ms. Perkins at the PCA reception desk shares a surname with three people already documented in the network:

NameRoleConnection
Todd PerkinsBanks’ personal attorneyPerkins Law Group, Detroit. Represented Judge Miller in DTW gun case.
Judge Sean Perkins36th District CourtTodd’s brother. Worked at Todd’s firm before the bench.
Judge David Perkins3rd Circuit CourtFamily donated to Banks-aligned campaigns.

Three Perkins in the legal/judicial layer protecting Banks. One Perkins at the school reception desk denying access to a parent.

Is Ms. Perkins related to Todd and Sean Perkins?

We don’t know yet. The surname match is documented. The question is asked. The answer will come from the sweep.

What the Law Says

FERPA (20 U.S.C. §1232g): Custodial parents have the right to access their children’s education records and information about their children at school.

MCL 380.1137: Schools shall not deny a parent access to their child except by court order.

MCL 600.916: It is illegal to represent yourself as an attorney if you are not one. Banks did this on August 29 to justify denying access. DPD Report #26-0909-0176 documents it.

A receptionist saying “I haven’t seen anybody” is not a legal basis for denying a parent information about their child. It is a lie designed to end the conversation.

Call the Number

(313) 767-3100

Ask for Brian Banks. Ask about your child. Listen to what they tell you.

Then read this page again.

Verify Everything

Banks has 9 convictionsICHATSID 2029469K at michigan.gov/msp
PCA phone numberPCA websitepurposecharteracademy.com/contactus
Todd Perkins is Banks’ attorneydetroit.primals.eco/network/professional-enablers/todd-perkins/
Sean Perkins is Todd’s brotherdetroit.primals.eco/network/judges/sean-perkins/

Connected Analysis

  • They Banked on Banks — 9 convictions, 2 charter schools, the full record
  • The Enforcement Ecosystem — 10 oversight bodies, none coordinated, none acted
  • Signal Permeability — Live measurement: Snyder responded in 13 minutes with her personal cell. JTC sent a form letter. Ms. Perkins said she hasn’t seen anybody.

entry.title: Anderson Permeability — When Institutions Lose Their Membranes
entry.content:
Lens: 🕸️ Topology ⚛️ Lattice 📅 Chronology 💰 Money ⚖️ Legal 🏛️ Capture

From Localization to Permeability

The Anderson Localization analysis showed how disorder in the judicial lattice traps cases — like electrons in a disordered crystal, cases entering captured courts cannot propagate to fair hearings.

This page documents a second phenomenon from the same physics: Anderson permeability — when the membranes between institutions dissolve entirely.

In condensed matter physics, a membrane’s permeability determines what passes through it. A healthy cell membrane is selectively permeable: nutrients in, waste out, toxins blocked. When the membrane fails — when everything passes through — the cell dies.

Institutions have membranes too:

MembraneWhat It Should BlockWhat It Should Allow
CredentialUnqualified staffCredentialed educators
AuthorizationAuthorizer staff at authorized schoolIndependent oversight
GovernanceConflicts of interestIndependent board members
DynastyFamily concentration in one enterpriseMerit-based hiring
EnforcementContinued operation after findingsInvestigation → correction
TransparencyHidden staff, unlisted employeesPublic accountability

This page measures each membrane.

Membrane 1: Credential 📄 Documented

The credential membrane should block unqualified individuals from teaching children or managing schools. It is maintained by MOECS (Michigan Online Educator Certification System) and MCL 388.1763.

Measurement

Jason PerryPCA StaffNot in any database. Convergence score = 0.Unknown

Credential membrane status: BREACHED. See: Full credential audit

Membrane 2: Authorization 📄 Documented

The authorization membrane should separate the authorizer (DPSCD) from the authorized (Banks’ schools). This boundary ensures independent oversight — the people granting the charter are not the people running the school.

Measurement

Membrane 3: Governance 📄 Documented

Membrane 4: Dynasty 📄 Documented

Measurement: Three Dynasties

The Permeability Map

BANKS ENTERPRISE — ALL MEMBRANES

                Fake J.D. Tourism degree. Expired cert.

                6 bodies. 0 corrections.
                Two letters, one day apart, each pointing
                at the other office.

 TRANSPARENCY   ████████░░  OPAQUE (PCA)
                No staff page. 2 ghost nodes.
                COVID teleconference since 2020.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 OVERALL:       TOTAL PERMEABILITY
                The institution has no functional membranes.
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Anderson Localization + Anderson Permeability

The two Anderson phenomena work together:

PhenomenonDomainEffect
LocalizationCourtsCases trapped at captured benches — cannot propagate to fair hearing
PermeabilityInstitutionsMembranes dissolved — no boundary between authorizer and authorized, between family and enterprise, between oversight and operation

Localization traps the output (cases). Permeability removes the input filters (hiring, authorization, oversight). Together, they create a system where unqualified people operate unchecked institutions that generate cases trapped in captured courts.

PERMEABILITY (input)          LOCALIZATION (output)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━          ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
No credential check     →    Uncredentialed staff teach children
No authorization check  →    Authorizer staff run authorized school
No governance check     →    Judges sit on boards of school they oversee
No enforcement check    →    6 bodies find problems, 0 corrections
                              │
                              ▼
                         Cases generated
                              │
                              ▼
                    ┌─────────────────────┐
                    │  CAPTURED COURTS    │
                    │  ξ = 3.5 (Probate)  │
                    │  ξ = 7.2 (36th)     │
                    │  Case → trapped     │
                    └─────────────────────┘

The children at PCA and MacDowell — 90.9% economically disadvantaged, 99.2% Black — enter a school with no functional membranes, taught by staff with no discoverable credentials, governed by judges with conflicts of interest, authorized by an agency whose employees work at the school. If a parent contests this system, their case enters a court where captured judges sit on the same school boards.

The input has no filter. The output has no exit.

Connected analyses:
  • 🔬 Anderson Localization — judicial lattice disorder traps cases (companion analysis)
  • 🧬 Staff Data Braid — eight independent searches, convergent staff graph
  • 🧬 GLLG Data Braid — first Crump dynasty signal (Jehan + Verkeydia)
  • 📋 Credential Gap — MOECS audit of MacDowell staff
  • 🏛️ Institutional Capture — how the board was captured
  • 🔗 Enforcement Ecosystem — statewide enforcement gap

All measurements are derived from public records: school websites, LinkedIn profiles, MOECS public search, LARA entity records, ProPublica 990 filings, and court records. Problems originate in dynasties, move through entities, and land on humans. The humans are children. Verify everything.

entry.title: The Dykema Chronology — 1988 to Present
entry.content:
How to Read This

Every entry has a date, a source, and the actors/entities involved. The timeline traces one law firm’s connections across 36 years — from shelf corporations in 1988 to charter school board governance in 2026.

This is not a conspiracy theory. It is a public record.

Phase 1: Building the Legal Framework (1982–1997)

1982 — McLellan Joins Dykema

Richard D. McLellan’s private practice merges with Dykema Gossett. He becomes head of the Government Policy & Practice Group and Managing Member of the Lansing office. He had previously served on Gov. William Milliken’s staff.

Source: Wikipedia; McLellan biography, Mackinac Center.

Actor: Richard McLellan (Dykema partner, Lansing)

1987 — McLellan Co-Founds Mackinac Center

McLellan co-founds the Mackinac Center for Public Policy, a free-market think tank that will become the intellectual engine behind Michigan’s charter school movement. He serves as board secretary for decades.

Source: Mackinac Center

Actors: Richard McLellan, Joseph Olson

1988 — Dykema Registers Shelf Nonprofits

Dykema registers pre-formed nonprofit entities — empty corporate shells ready for activation:

EntityLARA IDFiledStatus
Dykema Gossett Nonprofit Shelf Corporation800865335Aug 16, 1988Dissolved
Dykema Gossett Shelf Nonprofit Club Corporation800797761Oct 7, 1988Dissolved

Filed by Cindy M. Wilder at 800 Michigan National Tower, Lansing (Dykema’s former Lansing office). Dissolved within months.

Source: Michigan LARA Business Entity Search

Entity: Dykema Gossett PLLC

1990 — McLellan Runs Engler Transition

McLellan serves as transition director for Governor-elect John Engler. This positions Dykema at the center of the incoming administration that will create charter schools.

Source: Wikipedia; Mackinac Center biography

Actors: Richard McLellan, John Engler

Oct 5, 1993 — Engler Proposes Charter Schools

Governor Engler proposes charter school legislation in a speech before a joint session of the Michigan Legislature.

Source: Founders Library

Actor: John Engler

Dec 3, 1993 — Dykema Writes the Charter School Law

SB 896, creating Part 6a of the Revised School Code, passes the Legislature. Richard McLellan and Leonard Wolfe of Dykema Gossett are the “leading legal architects” of the legislation.

McLellan personally conducted “12 hours of shuttle diplomacy” in the Senate Majority Leader’s conference room to negotiate a version that would survive constitutional challenge.

The law allows:

  • State universities, community colleges, ISDs, and school districts to authorize charter schools
  • For-profit management companies to operate charter schools
  • A 3% authorization fee (incentivizing authorizers to keep schools open)
  • No statutory authorizer evaluation system
  • Board members appointed without identity disclosure requirements

Source: Founders Library; MI Good Government; Dykema.com Education page

Actors: Richard McLellan, Leonard Wolfe (Dykema)

Jan 14, 1994 — Engler Signs PA 362

Governor Engler signs the charter school law. Michigan becomes the 9th state to enact a charter school law.

Source: Founders Library

Actors: John Engler, Richard McLellan, Leonard Wolfe

1994 — First Charter Schools Open

Central Michigan University becomes the first authorizer. Three schools open: Casa Maria Academy (Detroit), New Branches School (Grand Rapids), Northlane Math and Science Academy.

Source: CMU Center for Charter Schools

1997 — Dykema Defends the Law at Supreme Court

The Michigan Education Association challenges the constitutionality of PA 362. Dykema’s McLellan and Wolfe defend the law before the Michigan Supreme Court in Council of Organizations and Affiliates v. Engler, 455 Mich 557 (1997).

The Court upholds the law and orders state funding restored.

Court record lists: “Dykema, Gossett, P.L.L.C. by Richard D. McLellan, Lori M. Silsbury, and Leonard C. Wolfe, Lansing, for intervening Defendants-Appellants.”

Source: Justia; 455 Mich 557

Actors: Richard McLellan, Leonard Wolfe, Lori Silsbury (Dykema)

Phase 2: The Machine Operator Arrives (2009–2016)

2009 — Wilk Forms Larry Deshazor Community Fund

W. Alan Wilk begins his entity formation practice. First documented entity:

EntityLARA IDYear
Larry Deshazor Community Fund70654L2009

Source: Michigan LARA Business Entity Search

Actor: W. Alan Wilk (Dykema)

2011 — NERD Fund

Wilk serves as legal and compliance officer for Governor Snyder’s NERD Fund (New Energy to Reinvent and Diversify). The fund:

  • Raised $2.19M from undisclosed donors over 3 years
  • Paid Rich Baird’s $100K salary
  • Paid EM Kevyn Orr’s travel expenses
  • Shut down in 2013 after transparency criticism

Source: Detroit News, Nov 19, 2014

Actors: W. Alan Wilk (Dykema), Rick Snyder, Rich Baird, Kevyn Orr

2011 — Wolfe Lifts the Charter Cap

Leonard Wolfe “plays instrumental role” in SB 618 (signed Dec 20, 2011), which phases out the cap on university-authorized charter schools. Wolfe attends the signing ceremony with Governor Snyder.

This removes the 150-school limit that had constrained charter expansion since 1999.

Source: Dykema.com

Actors: Leonard Wolfe (Dykema), Rick Snyder

2012 — Banks Elected to State House; Wells-Stallworth Joins MacDowell Board

Brian Roderick Banks elected to the Michigan House of Representatives (D-Detroit). Serves as Chair of the Detroit Caucus.

Nicole Wells Stallworth appointed to MacDowell Preparatory Academy board. She will serve continuously for 14 years.

Source: purposecharteracademy.com; charterschools.org

Actors: Brian Banks, Nicole Wells Stallworth

2015 — Dykema Sues Ellison (Garcia v. Title Check)

Dykema represents the plaintiff in Garcia v. Title Check LLC (1:15-cv-00975, W.D. Michigan). Obtains $73,752.45 in sanctions against attorney Philip L. Ellison for litigation misconduct.

Banks and Ellison were MSU Law classmates (2010).

Source: PACER, W.D. Michigan

Actors: Philip Ellison, Dykema attorneys (unnamed)

Phase 3: Dark Money Pipeline Activates (2016–2021)

Sep 8, 2016 — Wilk Forms Save Detroit Jobs

W. Alan Wilk incorporates Save Detroit Jobs (LARA 802002459). Entity email: compliance@dykema.com. Same day, Wilk also incorporates Detroit Jobs First (per Metro Times, FCC filings).

SDJ board: Rev. James Holley (president, former Duggan civic liaison), Mike Allen (LIUNA Local 1191), Lisa Canada (MI Regional Council of Carpenters).

Both entities are created to fight Proposal A — a citizen-led community benefits ordinance in Detroit.

Source: Michigan LARA; Metro Times

Actors: W. Alan Wilk, James Holley, Mike Allen, Lisa Canada

Nov 2016 — SDJ Pays Carol Banks $14,279; Pays Dykema $9,000

Save Detroit Jobs pays Carol Banks (chief of staff to Councilman Scott Benson) approximately $14,279 via ~70 separate reimbursements.

SDJ also pays Dykema Gossett nearly $9,000 in legal fees.

SDJ raises over $100,000 from: Blue Cross Blue Shield, Turn Around Wayne County PAC (Matthew Moroun’s Central Transport), Schostak Family PAC (Republican). Renae Moore is recordkeeper for Turn Around Wayne County PAC.

Source: Free Press, Sep 22, 2021

Actors: Carol Banks, Scott Benson, W. Alan Wilk, Renae Moore

2017 — Banks Resigns from State House

Banks resigns from the Michigan House as part of a plea deal that allows him to avoid up to 14 years in prison for defrauding a credit union. He is convicted of 8 felonies (later updated to 9 total: 6 felony, 3 misdemeanor).

Source: Free Press, Aug 27, 2023

Actor: Brian Banks

Sep 2018 — Impact Detroit Assumed Name

SDJ registers assumed name “Impact Detroit” (LARA record). First persona change.

Source: Michigan LARA, Entity 802002459

2020 — Wilk Forms Our Neighborhoods First

Wilk incorporates Our Neighborhoods First (LARA 802493189). Officers include Keenann Knox (Impact Church), Lorna Thomas (Public Lighting Authority chair, Duggan appointee), Betty Brooks (ex-police commissioner, “dear friend” of Duggan for 30 years).

Renae Moore serves as both Dykema employee AND compliance officer for the Duggan campaign AND recordkeeper for ONF.

Source: Deadline Detroit

Actors: W. Alan Wilk, Keenann Knox, Renae Moore, Lorna Thomas, Betty Brooks

Aug 10, 2021 — Detroit Leaders Assumed Name

SDJ registers assumed name “Detroit Leaders” — one week after Latisha Johnson and Steve Elrick advance to the general election in District 4. Detroit Leaders sends mailers supporting Johnson against Elrick.

Source: Deadline Detroit

Actors: Latisha Johnson, Steve Elrick, Keenann Knox, W. Alan Wilk

Aug 25, 2021 — FBI Raids Carol Banks

FBI raids Carol Banks’ East English Village home as part of “Operation Northern Hook” — the public corruption investigation that produced Councilman Andre Spivey’s bribery conviction. Agents seek records on 501(c)(4) organizations and campaign financing.

Source: Free Press, Aug 25, 2021

Actor: Carol Banks

Nov 2021 — Johnson Wins, Elrick Loses

Latisha Johnson defeats journalist Steve Elrick in Detroit District 4. The dark money entity formed by Dykema’s Wilk helped defeat the journalist who covered Banks’s network.

Source: Wayne County election results

Actors: Latisha Johnson, Steve Elrick

Phase 4: The Board Is Captured (2022–2025)

Aug 2022 — Banks Applies for School Administrator Certificate

Ten days after losing his county commissioner race, Banks applies for a school administrator certificate from MDE. Granted the next day (Sep 2, 2022 — school starts Aug 29).

Source: Free Press, Aug 27, 2023; MDE records

Actor: Brian Banks

Feb 2022 — MDE Investigates Banks’s Credentials

MDE sends letter to Wells-Stallworth (MacDowell Board Chair) warning that Banks’s employment “may be in violation of the State School Aid Act.” Banks has no valid Michigan teaching credential.

MDE gives the school a procedural loophole rather than enforcing compliance.

Source: MDE FOIA response, Sep 25, 2026

Actors: Brian Banks, Nicole Wells Stallworth, MDE

Jun 2023 — Wells-Stallworth Defends Charter Board Governance

Wells-Stallworth publishes Bridge Michigan op-ed: “Michigan charter school boards ensure financial accountability.” She presides over a board approving 72.67% revenue extraction to Banks’s management LLC.

Appears on MAPSA podcast: “A Charter School Board Member Tells All.”

Source: Bridge Michigan, Jun 9, 2023

Actor: Nicole Wells Stallworth

Jun 2023 — Wilk Forms Put Progress First

Wilk incorporates Put Progress First — a nonprofit backing Duggan’s leadership, signaling a possible gubernatorial bid. Same Dykema formation pattern.

Source: Bridge Detroit

Actors: W. Alan Wilk, Mike Duggan

Aug 2023 — Free Press “Back to Fool”

M.L. Elrick publishes “Back to Fool” — exposing Banks as an 8-time felon hired as principal of MacDowell. Board members had donated to Banks’s 2022 county commissioner campaign before hiring him.

Source: Free Press, Aug 27, 2023

Actor: M.L. Elrick, Brian Banks

Nov 2024 — Purpose Group LLC Filed

The Purpose Group, LLC (LARA 803295082) filed November 14, 2024. Sole member: Brian Banks. This is the management company that will receive 72.67% of school revenue.

Source: Michigan LARA

Actors: Brian Banks

Dec 2024 — Michigan Charter Reform Bills

Michigan legislature passes charter reform requiring authorizers to review contracts over $100K, attend 50%+ of board meetings, and mandate audited EMO financials. This legislation is directly responsive to governance failures like Banks’s operation.

Source: Chalkbeat, Dec 13, 2024

Jan 2025 — FBI Closes Carol Banks Investigation

FBI closes the public corruption investigation into Scott Benson and Janée Ayers without charges. Carol Banks is not charged.

Source: Free Press, Jan 17, 2025

Actor: Carol Banks

2025 — Purpose Charter Academy Authorized

DPSCD authorizes Purpose Charter Academy, citing “claimed improvement” at MacDowell. PCA board assembled:

PositionNameInstitutional Conflict
ChairJudge Cylenthia MillerWayne County 3rd Circuit — former Dykema attorney
Vice ChairLamar MorelandAsst Attorney General — AG could investigate Banks
SecretaryLatisha JohnsonDetroit City Council — Council oversees DPSCD

Johnson was elected with help from Detroit Leaders — the Dykema-formed entity. Miller is a former Dykema attorney. The board that governs a convicted felon’s school was ASSEMBLED using Dykema infrastructure.

Source: purposecharteracademy.com; DPSCD board minutes (Jul 2025); Chalkbeat, Sep 8, 2025

2025 — SDJ Funds Sheffield Mayoral Campaign

SDJ sends $84,500 to Detroit Next PAC, which runs $212,600+ in pro-Sheffield advertising. Sheffield wins. Appoints Chief Bettison (who sits on DPSA board — another charter school board).

Source: TransparencyUSA; campaign finance filings

Actors: Mary Sheffield, Todd Bettison

Phase 5: The Investigation (2026)

Mar 2026 — Miller Announces PCA Board Role

Judge Miller publicly announces her role as PCA Board Chair on LinkedIn: “I am so honored and proud to serve as the Chairperson of the Board of Directors of this amazing new school.”

Source: LinkedIn

Actor: Cylenthia Miller

Sep–Oct 2026 — Investigation Goes Live

  • Sep 13: Clutch Justice publishes MacDowell investigation
  • Sep 21: FOIA filed with MDE
  • Sep 25: MDE responds confirming credential investigation
  • Oct 4: AGC complaints filed (Miller, Moreland)

What It Means

The staff structure reveals a pattern that the Anderson Localization analysis predicted in the judicial lattice: the membranes that should separate institutions have dissolved.

In the courts, captured judges prevent cases from propagating to fair hearings. In the schools, captured staff prevent the authorization boundary from functioning. The authorizer’s own employees run the authorized school.

The Crump surname signal — first identified in the GLLG data braid — now extends from legal defense through board governance to daily operations. If the family connection is confirmed, it represents the deepest dynasty embed documented in the investigation.

The two ghost nodes (Perry, “Giselle”) represent something the investigation has not encountered before: people who exist inside the institution but are invisible to every public database. Their convergence score of zero is itself a measurement. In physics, the absence of signal is data.

See also: Anderson Localization — when courts trap cases. Credential Gap — who teaches without credentials. GLLG Data Braid — the first Crump signal.

All sources are public records. LinkedIn profiles are publicly accessible. MOECS is a public state database. School websites are public. Verify everything.

entry.title: Institutional Response Tracker
entry.content:
From Courts to Checkpoints

The Anderson Localization analysis showed that captured judges create disorder in the judicial lattice. Cases that enter cannot propagate to a fair hearing.

But courts are not the only institutional checkpoint. Michigan has layered accountability structures: credentialing bodies, oversight commissions, authorizers, professional discipline departments, and law enforcement agencies. Each exists to catch what the others miss.

The question this page answers: When the same verified evidence is submitted to multiple institutional checkpoints simultaneously, which ones act and which ones don’t?

The answer reveals whether the accountability system functions or whether the disorder extends beyond the courts into the institutions designed to oversee them.

The Model

Every institutional checkpoint is a lattice site. Evidence arrives like an electron. Either the institution transmits it forward (investigation, action, referral) or it absorbs and traps it (closure, dismissal, non-response).

If every checkpoint absorbs, the system is fully localized. No accountability can propagate.

The measurement is simple:

InputWhat Was Submitted
SubjectBrian Roderick Banks: 9 criminal convictions (SID 2029469K), unauthorized use of “J.D.” credential, operation of two DPSCD-authorized charter schools
EvidenceICHAT criminal record, LARA corporate filings, MOECS credential audit, academic performance data (3% math proficiency), financial records ($4.9M revenue, 72.67% extraction to Purpose Group LLC), campaign finance data
FormatVerified public records, structured for independent verification
Sitedetroit.primals.eco

The same evidence package. Multiple institutions. Measure the output.

The Data

Checkpoint Response Table

This table is updated as responses arrive. Each row documents the institutional output for the same evidentiary input.

#InstitutionDepartmentFiledResponseDaysResult
1Michigan Dept. of EducationEducator Excellence20222022–Cleared with conditions
2Detroit Public Schools CDBoard of DirectorsJul 2025Jul 2025–Authorized second school
3State Bar of MichiganUPL Dept. (File 26-UP-51)Aug 2026Sep 30, 2026~30Administratively closed
4State Bar of MichiganUPL (2nd complaint)Sep 2026–PendingAwaiting response
5Baker CollegeHuman ResourcesOct 2026Oct 5, 2026<2Permanently severed
6Attorney Grievance CommissionProfessional discipline (x7)Sep-Oct 2026–PendingInvestigations pending
7Judicial Tenure CommissionJudicial conductSep 2026Sep 2026~5Investigations opened
8Central Michigan UniversityCharter authorizationPending––Notification staged
9MDE (Round 2)Credential re-examinationPending––Notification staged
10Detroit Inspector GeneralMunicipal oversightPending––Complaint staged

Key Observations

The only institution that acted in under 48 hours was a private employer with no regulatory obligation.

Baker College reviewed the same evidence that Michigan’s credentialing body, authorizing district, and professional bar department reviewed. Baker permanently severed ties. The regulatory bodies either cleared him, authorized him, or closed the complaint.

The UPL Department’s stated reason for closure: “Does not meet the standards set by the Unauthorized Practice of Law Committee to pursue this matter further.” The subject uses “J.D.” in professional communications, holds no bar admission in any jurisdiction, and operates a school named “School for Law and Public Service.”

The UPL Department’s stated alternative: “You may have other remedies available to you.”

The UPL complaint was the first of several submitted as the scope of the unauthorized credential use became clear through the investigation. Additional complaints remain pending and will be updated here as responses arrive.

The Asymmetry

Michigan’s system demands active defense from individuals:

  • A parent must file a motion and appear at a hearing to see their own children
  • A citizen must file an affirmative defense within 14 days to contest a personal protection order
  • A pro se litigant must meet the same procedural standards as a licensed attorney
  • A victim of assault must obtain and serve their own police report
  • A custody case requires the responding parent to affirmatively request the investigation the filing parent opted out of

But when a citizen uses the system’s own accountability tools:

  • A UPL complaint against a 9-time convicted felon using “J.D.” is closed as not meeting standards
  • An administrator certification for a habitual offender is granted with conditions
  • A second charter school is authorized for an operator whose first school ranks in the bottom 3% statewide
  • A police report filed at the scene of an assault requires the victim to drive to the precinct to retrieve it

The system enforces process against citizens aggressively. It declines to enforce against its own members passively.

This asymmetry is not incidental. It is the localization.

When the disorder in the lattice extends from the courts into the oversight bodies, the accountability signal has nowhere to propagate. Every checkpoint absorbs it. The individual is left with “other remedies available to you,” which means: the system has told you it will not help.

The Measurement Continues

This page is a living document. As institutional responses arrive, the table updates. Each response or non-response is a data point in the same experiment.

The question is not whether any single institution failed. Institutions make judgment calls. The question is whether the pattern of non-response across multiple independent checkpoints reveals structural localization rather than individual discretion.

When the same evidence produces action from a private college in 48 hours and produces closure from a state regulatory body in 30 days, the comparison is the finding. No editorial interpretation is required.

This is Anderson Localization measured in institutional responses rather than court assignments. The physics is the same: disorder prevents propagation. The measurement is how deep the disorder goes.

All submissions are documented. All responses are recorded as metadata. All claims are verifiable against public records. See Legal Protections for the First Amendment and fair comment framework.

Related: The pattern of institutions that ignore boundaries extends beyond Michigan oversight bodies. See Signal — Public Record of Automated Access for evidence of the same dynamic in corporate AI systems that access this investigation site: some check the rules and comply; others read the rules and scrape anyway.

entry.title: Every Person Named in Banks's Book — Network Map from His Own Words
entry.content:
What This Page Is

Brian Banks wrote a book. He named people. He described relationships. He confessed to behaviors — his own and others’. Every word is a party admission under Michigan Rule of Evidence 801(d)(2)(A) — his own published statement, admissible against him in pending litigation.

This page catalogs every person named in the book, identifies who they are using public records, and documents the relationships and behaviors Banks described in his own words.

Fair use notice: All excerpts are used for criticism, commentary, and public-interest reporting under 17 U.S.C. § 107. See the companion analysis for the full fair use framework.

The Judges — Three “Mentors” Who Are Sitting or Retired Jurists

Judge Denise Langford Morris — 42 References

Role per Banks: “my mentor” Actual role: Banks’s felony sentencing judge in Oakland County Circuit Court (~1999). Now retired. Wrote the book’s foreword.

Banks describes a relationship that progressed from judge-defendant to personal mentorship to campaign labor to credential endorsement:

  1. Sentenced Banks leniently (1-year probation, 6 months tether)
  2. Told Banks: “you need to get back in school and go to someone’s law school!” — while knowing his felonies would bar admission
  3. Met Banks for lunch at Brandy’s restaurant on Telegraph in Pontiac through mutual friend Roeiah
  4. Discussed her morning docket with civilians at the restaurant: Banks writes that “Judge Langford Morris was describing her morning docket to Roeiah and the other young lady and the various cases that she had heard.” A sitting judge describing active cases she heard that morning to non-lawyers at a restaurant.
  5. Invited Banks back to her courtroom and paraded him to staff
  6. Attended MSU Law BLSA events at Banks’s invitation
  7. Treated Banks to dinner when he “graduated from law school” — along with “several other judges”
  8. Banks volunteered on her Michigan Supreme Court campaign
  9. Wrote the foreword to a book branded “Brian Banks, J.D.” — endorsing the credential fraud of the felon she sentenced

What Banks confesses she did:

  • Discussed active cases with civilians in a restaurant (Canon 2, Rule 2.10 — Judicial Statements on Pending Cases)
  • Developed a personal ex parte relationship with a former defendant
  • Used a former felon defendant for campaign labor
  • Endorsed credential fraud in a published book foreword
📄 Documented

Judge Vonda Evans — 9+ References

Role per Banks: “my mentor,” campaign strategist, friend Actual role: Retired Wayne County Circuit Court judge

Banks writes: “Retired Judge Vonda Evans and I became friends almost sixteen years ago. Vonda and I met through a mutual attorney friend one summer while hanging out in downtown Detroit.”

What Banks confesses she did:

  • Coined “Bank on Banks” — the campaign slogan: “After going back and forth with several ideas, Vonda finally said, ‘I got it! Bank on Banks!’”
  • Provided campaign strategy advice for a nine-time convicted felon running for office
  • Arrived at Banks’s grandfather’s hospital with Judge Cylenthia Miller — demonstrating personal, not professional, relationship
  • Was present the night before the grandfather’s death alongside Gay-Dagnogo
  • Banks describes her as “the queen of unorthodox campaigning” who “would unintentionally campaign even when her elections were years away”
📄 Documented

Judge Cylenthia LaToye Miller — 7 References

Role per Banks: “my mentor,” “like family,” “big sister” Actual role: Sitting 3rd Circuit Court Judge. PCA Board President (LARA Entity 900072324). JTC complaint filed.

Banks writes: “She was a mentor for me while I was in law school and eventually became like family. We’ve watched each other grow and take prominent roles in the political world. From a district court judge to now a circuit court judge, I’ve been with her every step of the way.”

And: “my big sister, Cylenthia, and I survived.”

What Banks confesses she did:

  • Arrived at Banks’s grandfather’s hospital alongside Judge Vonda Evans — personal family crisis response by sitting judges
  • Maintained a “like family” relationship with a nine-time convicted felon while serving as a judge
  • Currently serves as Board President of a school operated by that same convicted felon
  • Banks’s description of watching “each other grow and take prominent roles” implies mutual support throughout both careers
📄 Documented

Judge E. Lynise Bryant

Role per Banks: Thanked as friend in acknowledgments Actual role: Wayne County judge

Judge Regina Thomas

Role per Banks: Thanked as friend in acknowledgments Actual role: Wayne County judge

The Inner Circle — Domestic and Economic Unit

Joseph Holland (“Joe”)

Role per Banks: “my best friend and brother… You’ve now become a permanent fixture in our family” Actual role: Three-time convicted felon. PAC treasurer (Bank on Banks PAC). Shares Banks’s mailing address. Domestic/economic partner.

Banks describes Holland at every major life event:

  • Present at master’s graduation
  • First call when the FBI arrived: “I called Joe, who was at work, and told him what had just taken place and asked him to meet me at the lawyer’s office at 11 a.m.”
  • Went to attorney Ben Gonek’s office together — shared legal crisis response
  • Cut Banks’s grandfather’s hair in the casket: “Joe and I returned to the funeral home a day or so later so Joe could give my grandfather one last haircut.”
  • Present at hospital alongside sitting judges

This is not a business relationship. This is a domestic/economic unit described in the defendant’s own published words.

📄 Documented

Roeiah — 33 References

Role per Banks: Friend, law school classmate, bridge to Langford Morris Actual role: The most frequently named character after Langford Morris. Attended MSU College of Law with Banks through the LEO Program.

Roeiah is the connective tissue of the entire Banks-judiciary relationship:

  • Met Langford Morris independently and “decided to exchange information”
  • Arranged the lunch at Brandy’s restaurant where Langford Morris discussed her docket
  • “Roeiah said, ‘Brian, this is your opportunity to let the judge know everything that you’ve done.’”
  • Toured MSU Law with Banks, met Mary Ferguson and Dean Alsup together
  • Both entered the LEO Program (designed for students who needed “an extra push”)
📄 Documented

The Political Network

Sherry Gay-Dagnogo

Role per Banks: Friend for “over twenty-four years through church,” fellow State Rep, “two of a kind” Actual role: Former DPSCD Board member who voted to approve PCA charter. Now Detroit City Ombudsman. The DPSCD-to-Ombudsman move is the quid pro quo. AGC complaint filed.

Banks writes: “No one would ever know if we had a disagreement because whenever we do not agree, we align on a matter before we’re in front of others.”

What Banks confesses she did:

  • Was present at the hospital the night before Banks’s grandfather died — alongside Judge Vonda Evans
  • The 24-year church friendship predates all political positions
  • Banks describes coordinated public-facing behavior: “we align on a matter before we’re in front of others”
📄 Documented

Tenisha Yancey

Role per Banks: Elementary school friend, same street, same schools Actual role: Sitting Wayne County Circuit Court judge. Succeeded Banks in his Michigan House seat.

Banks writes:

“One of my elementary school friends was Tenisha. Tenisha and I lived on the same street and went to elementary and high school together.”

“Currently, we live one street over from each other”

“This is the same Tenisha who succeeded me after I resigned from office.”

What Banks confesses about her — in his own published words:

“As a young adult, Tenisha ended up having some troubles of her own which caused her to spend a month or two in jail. Luckily, we both got our stuff together and Tenisha graduated and received her bachelor’s and law degrees. She then became an assistant prosecuting attorney even with felonies and misdemeanors.”

A sitting judge who Banks states had “felonies and misdemeanors” and “spent a month or two in jail.” Banks published this. It’s his party admission about a member of his network. Her sister operates his school. They still live one street apart.

📄 Documented

Thomas Stallworth IV (“Tommy”)

Role per Banks: Mentor, State Rep colleague What Banks describes: Met to discuss expungement law. Stallworth brought Banks to a meeting with Governor Rick Snyder. “Come with me… we’re headed to a meeting with Governor Rick Snyder.”

Latisha Johnson

Role per Banks: Thanked as friend in acknowledgments Actual role: PCA Board Secretary. Detroit City Council member. Campaign received payments from the same vendor network.

Commissioner Jewel Ware

Role per Banks: Thanked as friend Actual role: Wayne County political network. Note: volunteer Margaret Ware also thanked separately.

Wayne County Clerk Cathy Garrett

Role per Banks: Thanked as friend Significance: County-level institutional access through personal friendship.

Karen Dumas

Role per Banks: Thanked as friend Actual role: Detroit media/communications figure. Media access node.

Mildred Gaddis

Role per Banks: Thanked as friend Actual role: Detroit radio host. Media access node.

MSU College of Law — The Gateway

Mary Ferguson

Role per Banks: Director of Diversity Services at MSU College of Law What Banks describes: Ferguson met Banks and Roeiah immediately after their admissions tour. “Hi, I’m Mary Ferguson. I’m the Director of Diversity Services at the College of Law.” She shepherded both into the LEO Program and shared “portions of our story” with Dean Alsup.

Significance: Ferguson is the person who facilitated a nine-time convicted felon’s entry into law school. She advocated for his admission.

Dean Connell Alsup — 21 References

Role per Banks: African-American dean at MSU College of Law, supporter What Banks describes: “Dean Connell Alsup asked us a few questions about our journey and our desire to attend law school… Dean Alsup seemed immediately interested. Mary and Dean Alsup both said that we would make good candidates for the LEO Program.”

Banks names Alsup 21 times. The dean became a recurring presence throughout Banks’s law school experience.

Professor Mulligan — 14 References

Role per Banks: Contracts professor at MSU Law What Banks describes: A major figure in the law school narrative. Banks names him 14 times — more than most friends and family.

Professor Filiatrault

Role per Banks: MSU Law professor What Banks describes: Named once in the law school narrative.

Miss Linda

Role per Banks: Admissions staff at MSU Law What Banks describes: First point of contact for campus tour.

The BMF Connection

Tonesa Welch (“Toni” / “Aunt Toni”)

Role per Banks: Step-aunt Actual role: BMF Defendant #22 in USA v. Flenory et al. Banks’s biological father is also a BMF defendant.

Banks writes:

“my Step-aunt Toni got into some trouble with her then boyfriend, ‘T.’” “my aunt was a part of the internationally known group called ‘Black Mafia Family’ better known as ‘BMF’” “I, along with many other family members and friends, accompanied Toni to court on her sentencing day.” “She would often call and speak with my grandfather” “Toni and I frequently emailed each other and I flew out there one time to see and check on her.” “To this day, Toni and I remain close.”

Active, ongoing, maintained relationship with a convicted member of one of the largest drug trafficking organizations in American history. Documented by the defendant in his own published autobiography.

📄 Documented

Marvin Stokes — Banks’s Biological Father

Role per Banks: Biological father, discovered through a birth certificate What Banks describes: Banks discovered his father’s identity when he saw a birth certificate belonging to “Felicia” — a fellow church member — that listed “Marvin Stokes” as father. Banks and Felicia share the same father.

Banks grew up calling O.D. Banks “the only father that I really knew.” The biological father Marvin Stokes was absent.

The Legal Professionals

Mr. Condino — 9 References

Role per Banks: Defense attorney in Oakland County felony case What Banks describes: Represented Banks before Judge Langford Morris. Negotiated the plea deal that resulted in probation and tether.

Ben Gonek — 2 References

Role per Banks: Attorney retained when FBI/AG arrived What Banks describes: Banks and Holland went to Gonek’s office together when the FBI showed up. “I proceeded to contact an attorney by the name of Ben Gonek… He advised me to come see him within the next hour.” Gonek recognized the FBI agent’s name from prior cases and scheduled a meeting.

Brian Schmidtke, Esq.

Role per Banks: Legislative staff Significance: A licensed attorney working under a person using “J.D.” credentials without bar admission.

Rebecca Fadel, J.D. / Kyle Giallonardo, J.D.

Role per Banks: Legislative staff Significance: J.D. holders who worked under a non-licensed supervisor who presented himself as “J.D.”

Jillian Martin, Esq. / Kristine Longstreet, Esq.

Role per Banks: Friends Significance: Licensed attorneys in Banks’s social network who would have known — or should have known — about his bar status.

The Church and Spiritual Network

Bishop J. Drew Sheard / Karen Clark-Sheard

Role per Banks: Pastor and First Lady Actual role: Greater Emmanuel Institutional Church of God in Christ. The Clark Sisters are one of the most prominent gospel music families in America. Significance: Spiritual institutional cover.

Rev. Valerie M. Messiah (July 18, 1966 – March 29, 2020)

Role per Banks: “great encourager, supporter, and friend” What Banks describes: Lost to COVID-19 in March 2020. Banks: “believing that I could solve and handle anything.”

Pastor Ronald “Bishop” Alexander / Elder Robert Moore

Role per Banks: Thanked as friends in acknowledgments.

Campaign, Business, and Media

Role per Banks: Graphic and digital media team for the book Actual role: Banks’s Senate campaign payee ($9,400 per campaign finance records).

DeShon Gale — DG Creative Studios

Role per Banks: Book cover designer Significance: Designed the cover that says “Brian Banks, J.D.” — the primary visual instrument of the credential fraud.
